title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The enhanced access to high-quality health and nutrition services programme in Bangladesh implemented by Concern Worldwide aims to contribute to improved resilience of populations in Cox's Bazar living in camps for the displaced. The objective of the programme is to improve the nutritional status of children, adolescent girls and pregnant and lactating women; to support refugees and host communities to prepare for and respond better to shocks such as floods, landslide and cyclones; and to improve the capacity of national partners and other community structures to implement emergency nutrition and security interventions. . OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: To contribute to improving access to and availability of health, nutrition and DRR services for camp populations and host communities. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: One of the main objecives of the programme is to improve the nutritional status of children, adolescent girls and pregnant and lactating women and the CHC programme primarily supported ongoing nutrition programmes in the Rohingya refugee camps. Key interventions include the early detection of malnutrition through community-based screening, utilizing tools such as MUAC and oedema assessments at the household level. Malnourished children and pregnant or lactating women were then referred to nutrition centres for appropriate treatment. Additionally, the programme addresses the nutritional needs of infants under six months through the MAMI (Management of At-Risk Mothers and Infants under Six Months) Care Pathway, promoting exclusive breastfeeding and proper nutrition for both infants and their mothers. Social and behavioral change is addressed through mother-to-mother support groups, with a specific focus on pregnant and lactating women. These groups provide education on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF), along with counseling and messaging to improve nutritional practices. Furthermore, we work to improve the dietary diversity of the target group through homestead gardening initiatives which focuses on female participants.
